newsitem.title: UK: British workers better off than most in EU - study.
newsitem.headline: British workers better off than most in EU - study.

text.p: The average British employee earning around 6.80 pounds (about $11) an hour ends up with more money in his pocket than most of his European couterparts, including the Germans, a British survey showed on Monday.

"For many years, the general impression has been that UK employees enjoyed a lower standard of living than in other parts of central and northern Europe," said David Formosa, international research manager at consultants Sedgwick Noble Lowndes who conducted the survey.
"This is certainly not borne out by the figures today," Formosa said.
The survey, a Guide to Employee Benefits and Labour Law in Europe, showed that only workers in Luxembourg, Austria and Ireland receive more in net pay than the British.

The research, which compared average earnings across Europe taking into account deductions for income tax and contributions to pensions and welfare benefits, put Luxembourg top of the league with average net hourly earnings of 7.40 pounds.
Austria, with an average 7.10 pounds an hour, and Ireland with an average hourly wage of 7.00 pounds followed.
Germany, however, was seventh in line with workers earning 6.5 pounds net, coming behind Spain where employees took home an average 6.80 pounds.
The study showed that for the average British employee, deductions from gross earnings were 25 percent. This compared with Germany and Denmark where deductions of 33 and 38 percent were the mean.
"Other countries may offer higher gross salaries, but this does not mean that their citizens are always better off," Formosa said.

Nevertheless, while employees in Portugal had the lowest percentage deducted from their salaries, just 18 percent, their average gross pay level was still too low to lift it off the bottom of the net pay league, the survey said.
It showed Portuguese employees were the net pay paupers, receiving an average take-home salary of just 3.20 pounds an hour. ($ = 0.629 British Pounds)
